answers.question: Which contractor has a portfolio site with 15 years of contract left and a 20 MW firm residual, and would an export-credit agency guarantee a first unit?
answers.finding: Zenith Energy's own portfolio already has the shape the prospect asks for, and has already used the guarantee instrument. Kathleen Valley (Liontown Resources) has been operating since early 2024 under a 15-year PPA signed December 2022, with a 27 MW gas plus 5 MW diesel firm-thermal residual (32 MW total) and about 13 years of term left; Export Finance Australia already provided a A$25 million guarantee facility for that PPA. Zenith's July 2024 Mt Weld deal (Lynas Rare Earths) is a second qualifying site: a 15-year PPA whose term starts on commercial operation of the wind farm, scheduled for calendar 2026, with a 22 MW firm-thermal residual (17 MW gas, 5 MW diesel). Zenith's December 2025 KCGM deal with Northern Star Resources is larger still: a 25-year PPA including a Zenith-Northern Star joint venture supplying 120 MW of thermal generation, commissioning targeted for mid-2027. Aggreko's 16-year Syama contract (Resolute Mining, signed December 2019, 40 MW firm thermal) and EDL's 10-year Agnew contract (Gold Fields, 25 MW firm thermal) both clear the 15 MW firm-thermal bar but have roughly 9 and 3 years of term left respectively, short of the 10-year-remaining threshold. No TUGLIQ site in the same class was found.

answers.question: Which vendors is SRC evaluating now, and is the CA$80M still appropriated?
answers.finding: No public source names a successor vendor, extending the prior pass's finding. At the same April 15, 2026 Economy Committee hearing, SRC president Mike Crabtree added new detail not previously captured: about a dozen eVinci staff were reassigned ('we have taken the key folks and distributed them around other parts of SRC') and the project is effectively on pause while SRC continues to 'identify and progress' unnamed alternative microreactors; no RFI, RFP, or named vendor appears anywhere in the transcript. The 2026-27 Estimates volume itself (the actual budget document, not just news coverage of it) shows SRC's total appropriation dropping to $45.229 million for 2026-27 (Vote 35: $19.229 million operating plus $26.0 million capital transfers) from an $87.423 million FORECAST for 2025-26 (though 2025-26 had itself originally been ESTIMATED at only $19.423 million) -- a swing consistent with a large one-off capital item tapering off, but the Estimates volume's own line-item text is generic ('supports applied research and assists clients...') and never names the microreactor or the $80 million fund, so this cannot be read as direct confirmation either way. The only dated release found with a specific microreactor dollar figure -- 'an additional $21.5 million for SRC to pursue its commercial demonstration of a microreactor' -- is dated March 20, 2024 and belongs to the 2024-25 budget. No CNSC filing specific to the microreactor has been made since the cancellation: the only 2026 CNSC action naming SRC is a May 2026 licence renewal for SRC's unrelated Gunnar historic uranium mine and mill site, which the Commission's release states 'authorizes SRC to conduct ongoing remediation at the Gunnar site' and explicitly does not authorize any new activities.

answers.question: How many metric tons of uranium does each vendor's first-core plan need at $50-80 million a ton, and what did Standard Nuclear price into the Radiant and Antares contracts?
answers.finding: Per-vendor first-core fuel mass is starting to surface in company disclosures, though most Janus/ANPI vendors still do not publish it. Oklo's July 2023 SEC-filed investor presentation states an 'Initial fuel load of 4,750 kg' (with 2,375 kg refueling loads every 10 years) for its base 15+ MWe Aurora design -- Oklo uses HALEU metal fuel, not TRISO, so Standard Nuclear's $50-80 million per MTU TRISO price does not directly apply to it. Among TRISO-fueled vendors: BWXT delivered a full first core for Project Pele as 40,000 TRISO fuel compacts (total kg or MTU not disclosed); Radiant's Kaleidos first core was completed with at least 50 kgU of Standard Nuclear TRISO fuel delivered in Q2 2026 plus an undisclosed additional 'balance of the reactor core' delivered after quarter-end, so the true first-core total is higher than 50 kgU; and Antares' Mark-0 test reactor is 'loaded to less than 120 kilograms total for the reactor's operational life' of HALEU TRISO fuel. Kairos Power's Hermes NRC environmental report states a required start-up fissile inventory of 'no greater than 25 kilograms (kg) 235U' -- a fissile-mass figure, not a total fuel or MTU mass, and this pass could not get that NRC PDF to render as text, so it is carried as snippet-only. No first-core mass was found for X-energy's Xe-100 (only a facility-level ratio: its TX-1 plant's 5 MTU/year capacity is described as enough to fuel 'up to 11 Xe-100 reactors'), General Atomics' GA-TES, or Westinghouse's eVinci beyond unconfirmed 40-45 kg test-quantity mentions that could not be tied to a fetched primary source this pass.

answers.question: the primary source for Oklo's stated first-unit cost and its expected $/MWh, and the slide behind the DOE clean-firm band ($63-99 gas with carbon capture, $66-109 advanced nuclear, $69-119 renewables plus storage) that a reporter attributed to an Oklo shareholder presentation. State whether only the reporter's reading exists.
answers.finding: The $145 million figure still has no primary document tying it to a specific MWe rating: Oklo's most recent Form 10-Q (period ended June 30, 2026) restates only that the Aurora powerhouse line is 'designed to produce between 15 and 75 megawatts of electricity ("MWe")' with no cost figure attached, and no DOE clean-firm slide was found in any 2026 filing either. But a different, earlier Oklo primary document does pair a cost to an MWe figure: Oklo's July 2023 investor presentation, furnished to the SEC as a Form 425 exhibit ahead of its SPAC merger, states an 'Initial plant construction cost of approximately $24.0 million (excluding initial fuel load)' for a '15+ MWe' Aurora 'Design... expected to be scalable to 50+ MWe.' That is the only fetched primary document this pass found anywhere in Oklo's public filings that ties a dollar figure to a named MWe capacity. No published per-unit price for Last Energy's PWR-20 or PWR-5, or for any other microreactor vendor, dated after 2026-09-02 was found; the closest large per-unit figure in the sector, Radiant's up to $750 million for 15 Janus units, is dated August 26, 2026 (before the cutoff) and is already carried in this dataset's news record.

cases.name: KCGM (Kalgoorlie "Super Pit") Renewables and Thermal Power Project
cases.capacity: 256 MW wind, 138 MW solar, 138 MW/300 MWh battery storage, plus a Zenith-Northern Star joint venture supplying 120 MW of thermal generation and a 132kV transmission network; commissioning targeted for mid-2027
cases.summary: Zenith Energy signed a 25-year PPA with Northern Star Resources, announced December 2025, to build what is described as Australia's largest renewable energy project for the mining sector at KCGM's Kalgoorlie operations: 256 MW of wind, 138 MW of solar and 138 MW/300 MWh of battery storage. Zenith and Northern Star also formed a joint venture to supply 120 MW of firm thermal generation as backup, plus a 132kV transmission network and substations, with commissioning targeted for mid-2027 subject to approvals.
cases.microreactor_read: The 120 MW firm-thermal joint-venture slice is six to eight 20 MWe-class units at a single site with 25 years of contracted term and a mine life Northern Star states as multiple decades — the longest-term, largest-residual off-grid mine opportunity found in this sector to date, and evidence Zenith will structure firm generation as its own joint venture rather than folding it into the renewables PPA.
